messages:
vic: Noticing a sharp uptick in GPU preemptions in ap-southeast1 since 04:10 UTC. Pod lifecycle shows Pending -> attach timeout -> scheduler preempt chain.

anya: Confirmed. `device_attach_duration_ms` p95 jumped to ~20s. Kernel conntrack count close to limit on several nodes (nf_conntrack_count ~129k).

kai: Affected jobs: fractional-GPU tiny-gang with `requiredDuringScheduling` nodeAffinity + hard anti-affinity. They refuse to share and force whole-node reclamation when attach delays occur.

vic: Immediate mitigations to try: 1) canary bump nf_conntrack_max on 10% nodes, 2) flip tiny-gang annotation to soft anti-affinity for 30m, 3) scale warm-pool by +1. Which do we want first?

anya: I'm rolling a privileged daemonset to set `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` on a 10% canary. Will monitor `conntrack_drops` and `attach_latency`.

kai: I'll draft a short-lived scheduler patch to honor `redwood.io/soft-tiny-gang=true` that downgrades anti-affinity during the incident. Canary it to 15% of tiny-gang traffic.

oncall: infra-bot created INC-2026-089: "apse1 attach latency -> eviction cascade" assigned to eng-platform. If canary doesn't reduce preempts in 20m, ops will provision +1 on-demand GPU node in ap-southeast1 for 12h.

vic: Long-term notes: scheduler should prefer compaction for fractional/GPU jobs (pack by fractional request, prefer labeled warm nodes, and surface fragmentation metrics). Place-holder ticket in backlog: PACK-1122.

anya: Canary applied. Initial metric snapshot in 5m and will update channel.

vic: Thanks — keep reactions light, annotate any observed user impact.
